overview: The Medford Brooks Estate Land Trust board discussed city relations and legal responsibilities regarding the manor and caretaker, approved donating a police call box to Arts Collaborative Medford, and planned capital work including winter building repairs and access drive projects funded by ARPA.

items.title: Police Call Box Donation
items.summary: Approved donating the carriage house police call box to Arts Collaborative Medford with the condition that Brooks Estate history be included in the project.

items.title: City of Medford Relationship and Legal Counsel Update
items.summary: The board reviewed a recent conference with the mayor and city legal counsel regarding municipal responsibilities for property maintenance, utilities, and the manor caretaker, agreeing to compile historical precedents and review the 1997 manager's agreement.

items.title: Financial Report
items.summary: Received a financial snapshot reporting approximately $82,000 in available funds along with upcoming expenses and anticipated grant reimbursements.

items.title: Manor Caretaker Transition
items.summary: Considered an out-of-court departure agreement proposed by the caretaker's elder services caseworker and decided to counter with a target move-out date of April 30, 2025.

items.title: Administrative Contractor Introduction
items.summary: Introduced Alba as the trust's new administrative contractor working through February on digital file organization, membership tracking, and an operations handbook.

items.title: Winter Manor Repairs
items.summary: Reported that the City Council approved an appropriation of $55,000 for emergency manor repairs, with contractor quotes pending for slate roof, boiler, and radiator work.

items.title: Access Drive Project and ARPA Funding
items.summary: Discussed strategies to deploy a $250,000 state ARPA earmark before June 30, 2025, focusing on tree clearing, grading, and daytime parking lot preparation near the carriage house.

items.title: Community Outreach and Promotion
items.summary: Discussed creating informational flyers and placing an advertisement in an NAACP breakfast program to increase community visibility and membership.
